newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish Metsa-Botnia says may raise pulp prices.
newsitem.headline: Finnish Metsa-Botnia says may raise pulp prices.

text.p: Finnish pulp producer Metsa-Botnia Oy Ab, owned by forest industry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy, said on Monday it may raise pulp prices in May.
"If the pulp market develops favourably we may raise pulp prices in May," Jyrki Yrjo-Koskinen, marketing director at Metsa-Botnia, told Reuters by telephone.
Yrjo-Koskinen said Metsa-Botnia would sell northern long-fibre pulp at its current $520 per tonne level until May 1.

Finnish media reported on Monday that American Georgia-Pacific and Stone Container were planning to raise the price of northern long-fibre pulp to $580 per tonne as of May 1 from current $520 per tonne.
Swedish forestry group Sodra also said on Monday it might raise pulp prices in mid-April.
Production halts in North America have helped to lower delivery volumes, which in turn increases the likelihood of price hikes, Yrjo-Koskinen said.
"I firmly believe that (pulp) stocks will decrease in April due to the massive curtailing of production," he said.
North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) March pulp stock figures are expected to be released at the end of this week or the beginning of next.
